inspiration: Circle as a shader, not a sprite: CircleShader.shadergraph exposes a border width and a body colour; its node names (Length, Comparison, Branch) suggest the disc is built from a distance test. Recreate with our own signed-distance disc and a soft band at the rim.

Wavy rim as its own sub-graph: WavyOutline.shadersubgraph keeps the ripple separate from the disc (file name only read), so the same rim can sit on any blob. Recreate with a time-driven noise rim that pulses with activity.

Hue-shifted shading: the shader graph uses RGB-to-HSV and HSV-to-RGB custom functions, which suggests shading by shifting hue and value rather than mixing toward black. Worth a try for a colourful, non-muddy body.

Layered procedural starfield: StarfieldBackground.cs draws a flat base, several large low-alpha discs for nebula patches, and generated stars, and redraws each frame (line 30 is one such disc). Recreate with seeded stars and soft nebula discs at different alphas for depth.

Palette by index, one colour per player: CircleController.cs and FoodController.cs each keep a static colour array (line 6). A small curated palette gives each avatar an identity without a colour picker.

Timed spawn and decay as data: the generated bindings list timer tables such as SpawnFoodTimer, CircleDecayTimer and CircleRecombineTimer (for example module_bindings/Types/SpawnFoodTimer.g.cs line 14). Pickups that spawn, decay and recombine on timers keep an arena moving.

Tiling parallax (names read only): RepeatingBackground.png (128x128) and a ParallaxBackground.cs script sit side by side in the Unity client, which suggests a cheap tiled-depth backdrop. The script body was not read.

briefs.label: Rim-pulse orb
briefs.why: A soft blob whose rim ripples reads as alive, and the pulse can signal activity without extra UI.
briefs.keep: Disc body with a separate wavy rim; hue-shifted shading; a border width that can change with state.
briefs.change: Noise-driven rim rather than a regular wave; an asymmetric inner core; our own palette and an inner highlight.

briefs.label: Drifting nebula backdrop
briefs.why: Big faint discs and seeded stars give a deep-space backdrop with depth for little cost.
briefs.keep: Low-alpha large discs; generated stars; redraw each frame.
briefs.change: A dim cloud band instead of centred discs; our own colour story; a parallax layer for the stars.

briefs.label: Timed mote pickups
briefs.why: Pickups that appear, fade and recombine on timers keep a play area busy and readable.
briefs.keep: Spawn and decay timers as data; small tinted pickups that merge.
briefs.change: Our pickups are drifting shards rather than static dots; their timing is tied to the map event cycle.

briefs.label: Palette-seeded avatar
briefs.why: Each player shows a distinct colour from a small palette, which makes crowded scenes readable.
briefs.keep: A curated palette indexed per player.
briefs.change: Derive the index from a hash of the player name instead of a fixed list; add a value shift for depth.
